name: SN74ALVC164245DGGR
title: SN74ALVC164245: 16-bit dual-supply level-shifting bus transceiver, 2.5 V to 3.3 V or 3.3 V to 5 V, 3-state outputs
summary: A Widebus 16-bit non-inverting transceiver made as two 8-bit sections, with port A on its own supply VCCA (2.3 V to 3.6 V) and port B on VCCB (3 V to 5.5 V). It moves data between a 2.5 V and a 3.3 V bus, or between a 3.3 V and a 5 V bus, in the direction DIR selects; an active-low OE per section puts both ports in high impedance. The control inputs are referenced to VCCA. Outputs drive ±24 mA at 3.3 V and propagation delay is at most 5.8 ns between 3.3 V and 5 V. SN74ALVC164245DGGR is the 48-pin TSSOP on a 2000-piece reel.
key_figures: 5.8 ns (VCCA = 3.3 V ± 0.3 V, VCCB = 5 V ± 0.5 V); 7.6 ns (VCCA = 2.5 V, VCCB = 3.3 V)
–24 mA / 24 mA at 3 V; –18 mA / 18 mA at VCCA = 2.3 V
TSSOP-48 (DGG), SSOP-48 (DL), 56-ball and 54-ball BGA MicroStar Junior

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: One 8-bit section joins two pieces of logic. A controller on the A side, fed from a regulated 3.6 V rail, drives OE and exchanges eight data lines with port A. Port B carries the same eight lines to a second controller, other logic or LEDs. A buffer drives DIR to choose the direction. The transceiver's supply comes from the same 3.6 V rail, with a bypass capacitor to ground.
notes: The 3.6 V rail feeds both VCCA and VCCB. Section 2 is not used.

operation.text: Sixteen non-inverting bus transceivers in two independent 8-bit sections, each with its own DIR and active-low OE; the two sections can be tied together as one 16-bit transceiver. With OE low, DIR high drives port B from port A and DIR low drives port A from port B. With OE high both ports of the section are in high impedance and the buses are isolated.

Port A and the control inputs run from VCCA (2.3 V to 3.6 V), port B from VCCB (3 V to 5.5 V). The intended pairings are 2.5 V on A with 3.3 V on B, and 3.3 V on A with 5 V on B, so signals cross between 2.5 V and 3.3 V systems or between 3.3 V and 5 V systems in either direction. The DIR and OE thresholds follow VCCA.

The input buffers on both data ports stay on even while their outputs are disabled, so every data pin must sit at a defined high or low level; a floating or mid-level pin raises ICC and ICCZ. Unused inputs go to VCC or GND, and transceiver I/O pins may not float even when disabled.

Ground is connected before any supply, and VCCA, the control side, comes up first. OE is pulled up to VCCA through a resistor so it rises with VCCA and the outputs stay in high impedance while the supplies ramp; the smallest usable pull-up is set by how much current the driving gate can sink. DIR is held low unless the A-to-B direction is wanted, in which case it rises with VCCA. Ignoring the sequence risks excess supply current, bus contention and oscillation.

The balanced CMOS outputs source and sink up to 24 mA at 3.3 V. In bus contention that drive can push currents past the absolute maximum ratings, and into a light load the fast edges it produces can ring.

Each output carries no more than 50 mA and the whole part no more than 100 mA. Outputs are not pulled above their VCC. Input edges stay within the Δt/Δv limit and inputs meet VIH and VIL of the recommended operating conditions.
Tested to JESD 17, the part withstands latch-up currents above 250 mA.
